resolutions.researcher_notes: EIA 'Today in Energy' (Aug 24, 2020): 'Sendero Carlsbad Gateway Project: This new pipeline was completed in May 2020 and connects natural gas processing plants in southeastern New Mexico to the Waha hub.' Confirms the line is built and completed (i.e. operating). Second, distinct-publisher source: WhiteWater Midstream's own 'Carlsbad Gateway Pipeline' asset overview map (hosted on whitewatermidstream.com/assets, dated 2/11/2022, verified via Wayback since the live site is a JS SPA that renders no static text) depicts it as a current, named WhiteWater pipeline asset running Sendero Carlsbad Plant Interconnect -> Agua Blanca Pipeline Interconnect, consistent with an operating in-network line nearly two years after the EIA completion date. Verified the PDF's text layer directly with pdftotext (title 'CARLSBAD GATEWAY PIPELINE', legend '24" Carlsbad Gateway Pipeline') since the automated substring screen only checks raw text extraction, which is sparse on a map graphic; contains_value set true based on that manual read, not the substring screen alone.

FERC's Gateway Project Environmental Assessment (Docket CP18-538-000, Jan 2019) describes 'approximately 23 miles of 24-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline' -- a natural gas pipeline. EIA's Today in Energy piece independently calls it a 'natural gas pipeline' carrying processing-plant gas to the Waha hub. Two distinct publishers (federal regulator + federal statistics agency, different offices/documents) agreeing on Fuel = Gas.

EIA (Aug 24, 2020): 'This new pipeline was completed in May 2020' -- supports StartYear1 = 2020. Only one corroborating source found for the specific completion YEAR; the FERC EA (Jan 2019) only gives a target in-service date of June 30, 2019 (superseded -- the certificate itself was not issued until Oct 2019, so the EA's target date is not evidence of actual start), and NaturalGasIntel's Oct 2019 article covers the certificate order, not completion. Searched: FERC EA, NGI article, the ICF/NM infrastructure report (only shows a Jul-19 FERC-filing date, not completion), WhiteWater's own site/news index (JS-rendered, no readable press-release text recoverable even via Wayback). No second source pinning 2020 found; single-source EIA reporting is credible (federal statistics agency) but not independently corroborated, so medium/not-independent per the tier rule.

Natural Gas Intel (Oct 14, 2019): 'Sendero Carlsbad Gateway LLC's 400 MMcf/d natural gas pipeline.' FERC EA (Jan 2019): 'about 400 million standard cubic feet of natural gas per day.' EIA (Aug 2020): 'capacity of 0.40 Bcf/d' (= 400 MMcf/d, prose/unit equivalence). Three distinct publishers (trade press, federal regulator, federal statistics agency) agreeing on 400 MMcf/d.

NGI: '23-mile, 24-inch diameter pipeline.' FERC EA: 'approximately 23 miles of 24-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline.' EIA: '23-mile, 24-inch pipeline.' Three distinct publishers agreeing on 23 miles.
Same three sources as Length: all state 24-inch diameter. NGI: '24-inch diameter pipeline.' FERC EA: '24-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline.' EIA: '23-mile, 24-inch pipeline.'

FERC EA: facilities in 'Eddy County, New Mexico' (from the Carlsbad Plant) to 'Culberson County, Texas' at a White Water meter station / Agua Blanca interconnect -- matches StartLocation=Carlsbad NM / EndState=Texas. NGI: 'processing plants in Eddy County, NM, to an interconnect with White Water Midstream LLC's Agua Blanca intrastate system in Culberson County, TX.' EIA explicitly names the far end: 'connects natural gas processing plants in southeastern New Mexico to the Waha hub' -- matches EndLocation = Waha Hub. Three distinct publishers agreeing on the Carlsbad, NM -> Waha Hub, TX route.

Searched hard, no source found stating a $45,000,000 project cost for this segment specifically. Checked: FERC's Gateway Project EA (CP18-538, Jan 2019 -- no cost estimate given in the impacts/need sections); the NGI Oct 2019 certificate article (mentions only a separate $100M Carlsbad cryogenic processing PLANT cost, not the pipeline); the ICF 'Economic Importance of NM Oil and Natural Gas Infrastructure' report (Sep 2019, table lists the project's capacity and in-service date but no cost column); EIA's Today in Energy completion note (no cost given); WhiteWater's own site (JS-rendered, no press release text recoverable). Ruling out a fabricated/GEM-only figure was not possible either way -- genuinely unresolved, not contradicted.

MPLX LP's FY2023 10-K, Exhibit 21.1 (List of Subsidiaries, filed with the SEC) lists 'Agua Blanca Pipeline, L.L.C.' as an MPLX subsidiary -- confirms Owner2 = MPLX. WhiteWater Midstream's own projects page (archived Oct 2021, shortly after WhiteWater's Aug 26, 2021 announced acquisition of Sendero's Gateway pipeline per the gem.wiki lead -- that announcement text itself was not independently recoverable, whitewatermidstream.com/news is a JS single-page app with no static press-release text even via Wayback) states: 'Agua Blanca is a Joint Venture with WhiteWater and MPLX' -- confirms Owner1 = WhiteWater Midstream. WhiteWater's own 'Carlsbad Gateway Pipeline' asset map (dated 2/11/2022, i.e. well after the 2021 acquisition) shows the Sendero Carlsbad Plant Interconnect line terminating at an 'Agua Blanca Pipeline Interconnect,' consistent with this segment now sitting inside the WhiteWater/MPLX Agua Blanca system. Two distinct publishers (SEC filing + WhiteWater's own site, corroborating each other on the WhiteWater+MPLX ownership structure) -- flagged CONCERN below on percentages.
CONCERN: none of the three sources states Owner1%/Owner2% splits for this specific segment (the sheet leaves Owner1%/Owner2% blank, consistent with unknown split) -- not a value contradiction, just noting the split itself is not independently sourced.
